ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: Seeing the Extraordinary in the Ordinary

fullPassage:
Creativity. When you hear this word, what instantly pops into your mind? You may think it is a quality that only artists and writers possess — some special talent you are either born with or without. Many people accept the idea that we can be divided into two groups: those who are creative and those who are not. This common belief, however, is far from the truth. Everyone has the ability to be creative. Finding creativity inside yourself just takes a little effort. Some artists, for example, spark their creativity by looking closely at ordinary objects. They try to discover the beauty hidden within these common objects and then turn them into works of art.

Look at these two paintings. Believe it or not, they both depict the same person, Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II. The one on the left might look familiar, as it is a standard style of portrait that you would see in a gallery or an art book. However, the one on the right, called Vertumnus, is very unconventional. Created by a 16th-century Italian painter named Giuseppe Arcimboldo, the painting shows striking creativity and originality. Fruits, flowers, and vegetables are arranged like the pieces of a puzzle to create a human head. A cherry and a mulberry become the dark eyes, while an apple and a peach act as the pink cheeks. This painting is representative of the artist's signature style of "composite portraits." He used plants, animals, and other objects to create many other portraits like this.

Another good example of Arcimboldo's unique creativity can be found in The Gardener, one of his "reversible" paintings. When viewed normally, it is just an ordinary still life of vegetables in a bowl. However, when flipped upside down, it is magically transformed into a smiling face! Experts have studied this painting, along with Arcimboldo's other reversible ones. Their research showed that he first painted them as still life paintings and then turned them upside down and made some adjustments to create faces. X-ray examination revealed that he sometimes changed the positions of some of the fruits and vegetables. Why did he make his paintings reversible? It was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element to his work by doing so. Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game, which brings them a sense of pleasure.

Each of Arcimboldo's works is a careful study of everyday objects. When he looked at typical objects, such as a bowl of vegetables, he saw the artistic and imaginative potential in them. His innovative approach to art inspired many great artists who came after him, including Pablo Picasso, Salvador Dalí, and René Magritte.

Take a look at this picture. Do you see a horse standing in a field? Or is it simply a collection of clothes hanging on a clothesline? This witty and amusing creation is actually a work of art created by the visual artist Helga Stentzel. Using everyday items, she creates playful visual illusions that force you to look twice in order to confirm what you have just seen. Her unique style has been called "household surrealism."

Stentzel is perhaps best known for her Clothesline Animals series. She got inspiration for the series while she was hanging her laundry. By simply adding some colorful clothespins and a dish towel, she was able to transform her black sweatshirt and dark grey pants into a horse. Other creations followed, including a brown cow standing on some hills and a zebra crossing the desert. All of these works were created from nothing more than laundry and household items.

Another series that highlights Stentzel's astonishing creativity is Edible Creatures. For this series, she arranges food items you can find in any kitchen to create cute animals. The stars of the series are Brad Pet and Crunchie, a pair of puppies made of sliced bread and lettuce respectively. Stentzel says she came up with the concept of Crunchie while putting together a salad for her family.

What do you think her secret is? Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills that allow her to make magic out of the ordinary. As a child, she would spend time staring at the patterns in the wood of her bed, trying to find different animal shapes. She admits that even today she stares at things longer than is acceptable in society. This keen observation is what enables her to continuously produce creative and imaginative works of art.

Creativity is not some kind of exceptional skill that belongs to exclusive groups of people. It is actually a part of our daily lives, a power that we can display anytime we choose to. Whether we realize it or not, we are constantly using our creativity to adapt, adjust, and rearrange the things around us. By doing so, we are turning the ordinary into something extraordinary — something that has never been seen before. Take a look at the things around you, but don't just give them a quick glance. Look carefully, and you might discover something that sparks your own imagination and creativity.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 예술가들은 평범한 사물을 가까이 봄으로써(looking) 창의성을 발휘한다. look → looking (전치사 by 뒤에 동명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① look → looking: 전치사 by 뒤에 동명사(-ing) 필요. by looking closely = 자세히 봄으로써
❌ ② hidden: 과거분사가 beauty를 수식 (숨겨진 아름다움). 정상
❌ ③ turn: try to + 동사원형. 정상
❌ ④ works: works of art(예술 작품들) 복수형 명사. 정상
det.tip: 전치사(by/of/in) + 동명사(-ing). by looking = ~함으로써. spark creativity by looking = 봄으로써 창의성을 발휘하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그녀의 독특한 스타일은 "가정용 초현실주의"라고 불려 왔다(called). calling → called (수동태 has been called)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ calling → called: has been + p.p.(과거분사) = 현재완료 수동태. 스타일이 '불리는' 것이므로 수동태 필요
❌ ① created: 과거분사가 a work of art를 수식 (만들어진 작품). 정상
❌ ② to look: force + O + to V (강제로 ~하게 하다). 정상
❌ ④ known: be known for (~로 알려진). 과거분사 정상
det.tip: has been + p.p. = 현재완료 수동태. has been called = ~라고 불려 왔다. calling(능동) vs called(수동)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Giuseppe Arcimboldo라는 이름의(named) 16세기 이탈리아 화가에 의해 그려졌다. naming → named (과거분사: ~라는 이름의)
det.analysis:
✅ ② naming → named: 화가가 '이름 지어진' 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 named 필요. naming은 능동 의미
❌ ① that: 목적격 관계대명사. portrait that you would see. 정상
❌ ③ like: 전치사 '~와 같은'. portraits like this. 정상
❌ ④ who: 주격 관계대명사. artists who came after him. 사람 선행사+주격. 정상
det.tip: named = ~라는 이름의 (과거분사). a painter named X = X라는 이름의 화가. naming(현재분사)은 '이름을 짓는' 능동 의미

questions.passage: What do you think her secret is? Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills ①<u>that</u> allow her to make magic out of the ordinary. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 예리한 관찰이 그녀가 지속적으로 창의적인 작품을 만들어내는 것을 가능하게 하는 것(what)이다. that → what (선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ that → what: 'This keen observation is ____ enables her...'에서 주어 보어 자리. 선행사가 없으므로 what(~하는 것) 필요. that은 선행사 필요
❌ ① that: It is ~ that 강조구문. 'it is her skills that allow' = 그녀의 기술이 바로 ~하게 하는 것이다. 정상
❌ ② staring: spend time + V-ing (시간을 ~하며 보내다). 정상
❌ ③ is: than 뒤에 생략된 주어(it)의 동사. 'longer than (it) is acceptable'. 정상
det.tip: what = the thing that (선행사 포함). 'A is what enables B' = A는 B를 가능하게 하는 것이다. that은 선행사 없이 단독 사용 불가

questions.passage: Another good example of Arcimboldo's unique creativity can be found in The Gardener, one of his "reversible" paintings. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그는 정물화를 뒤집어서 얼굴을 만들기 위해 약간의 조정(adjustments)을 했다. anxiety(불안) → adjustments(조정)
det.analysis:
✅ ② anxiety(불안) → adjustments(조정)가 원문. 얼굴을 만들기 위해 조정을 했다는 맥락
❌ ① transformed(변형된): 원문 그대로. 뒤집으면 얼굴로 변환
❌ ③ interactive(상호작용적): 원문 그대로. 상호작용적 요소를 추가
❌ ④ visual(시각적): 원문 그대로. 시각적 게임을 하는 느낌
det.tip: adjustments(조정, 수정) ↔ anxiety(불안, 걱정). make adjustments = 조정하다. 문맥상 '조정'이 적합

questions.passage: Creativity is not some kind of exceptional skill that belongs to ①<u>exclusive</u> groups of people. It is actually a part of our daily lives, a power that we can ②<u>overlook</u> anytime we choose to. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그것은 우리가 원할 때 언제든지 발휘할 수 있는(display) 힘이다. overlook(간과하다) → display(발휘하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ② overlook(간과하다) → display(발휘하다)가 원문. 창의성은 언제든 '발휘'할 수 있는 힘이라는 긍정적 맥락
❌ ① exclusive(배타적인): 원문 그대로. exclusive groups = 배타적 집단
❌ ③ extraordinary(비범한): 원문 그대로. ordinary → extraordinary 변환
❌ ④ glance(흘끗 봄): 원문 그대로. quick glance = 빠르게 흘끗 봄
det.tip: display(발휘하다, 보여주다) ↔ overlook(간과하다, 놓치다). 창의성을 '발휘'한다는 맥락에서 overlook은 부적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Arcimboldo는 진정한 창의성이 평범한 사물을 관찰하는 것(observing ordinary things)에서 나올 수 있음을 증명했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ observing ordinary things: 일상적 사물에서 예술적 잠재력을 본다는 글의 핵심 주제
❌ ① expensive art supplies: 비싼 재료가 아닌 평범한 사물 활용이 핵심
❌ ② formal academic training: 정규 교육이 아닌 관찰력이 핵심
❌ ③ mysterious natural phenomena: 신비로운 현상이 아닌 일상적 사물이 소재
det.tip: everyday objects / ordinary things = 일상적 사물. 글의 핵심: 평범한 것에서 비범한 것을 발견

Whether we realize it or not, we are constantly using our creativity to adapt, adjust, and rearrange the things around us. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: proves that only talented people are truly creative
sparks your own imagination and creativity
requires years of formal artistic education
confirms creativity is reserved for professionals

det.korean: 주의 깊게 보면 자신의 상상력과 창의성을 촉발하는(sparks your own imagination and creativity) 무언가를 발견할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② sparks your own imagination and creativity: 원문 마지막 문장 그대로. 글 전체 메시지 = 평범함 속 창의성 발견
❌ ① 재능 있는 사람만 창의적: 글의 첫 문장에서 정반대 주장 (누구나 창의적)
❌ ③ 정규 교육 필요: 교육 언급 없음
❌ ④ 전문가 전용: 글의 핵심 메시지와 정반대
det.tip: spark = 촉발하다, 불을 붙이다. 글의 결론: 주의 깊게 관찰하면 누구나 창의성을 발견할 수 있다

questions.passage: Another series that highlights Stentzel's astonishing creativity is Edible Creatures. For this series, she arranges food items you can find in any kitchen to create cute animals. The stars of the series are Brad Pet and Crunchie, a pair of puppies made of sliced bread and lettuce respectively. Stentzel says she came up with the concept of Crunchie while putting together a salad for her family.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Edible Creatures 시리즈는 빨래를 이용하여 동물을 만든다.
Brad Pet은 상추로, Crunchie는 식빵으로 만들어졌다.
Stentzel은 가족을 위해 샐러드를 만들다가 Crunchie 개념을 떠올렸다.
Edible Creatures의 주인공은 고양이 한 쌍이다.

det.korean: Stentzel은 가족을 위해 샐러드를 만들다가 Crunchie 개념을 떠올렸다. 원문 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 샐러드 만들다가 Crunchie 구상: 'came up with the concept of Crunchie while putting together a salad for her family' 원문 일치
❌ ① 빨래 이용: Edible Creatures는 음식(food items) 이용. 빨래는 Clothesline Animals
❌ ② Brad Pet=상추, Crunchie=식빵: 반대. Brad Pet=sliced bread, Crunchie=lettuce
❌ ④ 고양이 한 쌍: puppies(강아지 한 쌍)임
det.tip: Brad Pet = bread(빵) + pet = 식빵 강아지. Crunchie = crunch(아삭) = 상추 강아지. 이름에 재료 힌트가 있음

questions.passage: Created by a 16th-century Italian painter named Giuseppe Arcimboldo, the painting shows striking creativity and originality. Fruits, flowers, and vegetables are arranged like the pieces of a puzzle to create a human head. A cherry and a mulberry become the dark eyes, while an apple and a peach act as the pink cheeks. This painting is representative of the artist's signature style of "composite portraits." He used plants, animals, and other objects to create many other portraits like this.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 과일, 꽃, 채소가 퍼즐 조각처럼 배열되어 인간의 머리를 만든다.
체리와 뽕나무 열매가 어두운 눈이 된다.
이 그림은 "합성 초상화"라는 그의 대표적 화풍이다.

det.korean: Arcimboldo는 16세기 이탈리아 화가이다. 17세기 프랑스가 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 17세기 프랑스: 원문은 '16th-century Italian painter'. 세기(16→17)와 국적(Italian→프랑스) 모두 불일치
❌ ② 퍼즐 조각 배열: 'arranged like the pieces of a puzzle' 원문 일치
❌ ③ 체리+뽕나무=눈: 'A cherry and a mulberry become the dark eyes' 원문 일치
❌ ④ 합성 초상화: 'signature style of composite portraits' 원문 일치
det.tip: 16th-century = 16세기(1500년대). Italian = 이탈리아의. 세기와 국적 두 가지가 모두 변경됨

questions.passage: What do you think her secret is? Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills that allow her to make magic out of the ordinary. As a child, she would spend time staring at the patterns in the wood of her bed, trying to find different animal shapes. She admits that even today she stares at things longer than is acceptable in society. This keen observation is what enables her to continuous produce creative and imaginative works of art.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.

det.korean: 이 예리한 관찰은 그녀가 지속적으로(continuously) 창의적인 작품을 만들어내는 것을 가능하게 한다. continuous(형용사) → continuously(부사)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ continuous → continuously: produce(동사)를 수식하므로 부사 continuously가 필요
❌ ① allow → allows: 선행사가 skills(복수)이므로 allow가 정상
❌ ② staring → stare: spend time + V-ing (시간을 ~하며 보내다) 정상
❌ ③ longer → more longer: 비교급 longer 자체가 정상. more는 불필요
det.tip: 동사 수식 = 부사. continuously produce = 지속적으로 만들어내다. continuous(형용사)는 명사 수식

questions.passage: Stentzel is perhaps best known for her Clothesline Animals series. She got inspiration for the series while she was hanging her laundry. By simply adding some colorful clothespins and a dish towel, she was able to transform her black sweatshirt and dark grey pants into a horse. Other creations followed, including a brown cow standing on some hills and a zebra crossing the desert. All of these works were created from nothing more than laundry and household items.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"Stentzel은 그녀의 빨래줄 동물 시리즈를 위해 검은 맨투맨과 어두운 회색 바지를 __________(으)로 변신시킬 수 있었다."

det.korean: 검은 맨투맨과 어두운 회색 바지를 말(a horse)로 변신시켰다.
det.analysis: 원문 'she was able to transform her black sweatshirt and dark grey pants into a horse'에서 a horse를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: transform A into B = A를 B로 변환하다. sweatshirt + pants → horse

questions.passage: Creativity is not some kind of (exception) skill that belongs to exclusive groups of people. It is actually a part of our daily lives, a power that we can display anytime we choose to. Whether we realize it or not, we are constantly using our creativity to adapt, adjust, and rearrange the things around us. By doing so, we are turning the ordinary into something (extraordinary) — something that has never been seen before.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 올바른 형태로 바꾸시오.

(exception) →

det.korean: 창의성은 어떤 종류의 특별한(exceptional) 기술이 아니다. exception(명사) → exceptional(형용사)
det.analysis: exception(예외, 명사) → exceptional(예외적인, 형용사). skill(명사)을 수식하는 형용사가 필요.
det.tip: 명사 수식 = 형용사. exception(n. 예외) → exceptional(adj. 예외적인, 특별한). exceptional skill = 특별한 기술

questions.passage: Why did he make his paintings reversible? __________. Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game, which brings them a sense of pleasure.
questions.stem: (정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. to / an / add / he / interactive / wanted / element / probably / because / it / was
questions.wa: it was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element
accept: it was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element
It was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element
it was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element.
It was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element.

det.korean: 아마도 그가 자신의 작품에 상호작용적 요소를 추가하고 싶었기 때문일 것이다.
det.analysis: It was probably because + S + V: ~때문이었을 것이다. wanted to add an interactive element = 상호작용적 요소를 추가하고 싶었다.
det.tip: It was probably because ~ = 아마 ~때문이었을 것이다. add an interactive element = 상호작용적 요소를 추가하다

questions.passage: Creativity is not some kind of exceptional skill that belongs to exclusive groups of people. It is actually a part of our daily lives, a power that we can display anytime we choose to. Whether we realize it or not, we are constantly using our creativity to adapt, adjust, and rearrange the things around us. By doing so, we are turning the ordinary into something extraordinary — something that has never been seen before. Take a look at the things around you, but don't just give them a quick glance. Look carefully, and you might discover something that sparks your own imagination and creativity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 예술가가 되기 위한 전문 교육의 중요성
일상에서 누구나 발휘할 수 있는 창의성

det.korean: 창의성은 특별한 집단의 것이 아니라 일상에서 누구나 발휘할 수 있는 힘이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 일상 창의성: 'a part of our daily lives, a power that we can display anytime'. 글 전체의 핵심 메시지
❌ ① 전문 교육: 교육 언급 없음. 오히려 일상에서 자연스럽게 발휘 가능
❌ ③ 작품 감상법: 감상법이 아닌 창의성의 보편성이 주제
❌ ④ 미술 시장: 시장 언급 전혀 없음
det.tip: creativity = a part of our daily lives. 핵심 키워드: ordinary → extraordinary, everyone, daily lives

questions.passage: Some artists, for example, spark their creativity by looking closely at ordinary objects. They try to discover the beauty hidden within these common objects and then turn them into works of art. Arcimboldo used fruits, vegetables, and plants to create composite portraits and reversible paintings. Stentzel transforms laundry and food items into playful visual illusions. Both artists show that remarkable art can come from paying close attention to the world around us.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Artists like Arcimboldo and Stentzel demonstrate that ___(A)___ objects can be transformed into ___(B)___ works of art through keen observation.

det.korean: 일상적인(everyday) 사물이 예리한 관찰을 통해 비범한(extraordinary) 예술 작품으로 변환될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ everyday — extraordinary: 글의 핵심 대비 구조. ordinary/everyday → extraordinary
❌ ① exotic — traditional: 이국적 사물이 아닌 일상적 사물이 소재
❌ ② artificial — technical: 인공적/기술적이라는 맥락 없음
❌ ④ ancient — historical: 고대/역사적이라는 맥락 없음
det.tip: everyday(일상적인) ↔ extraordinary(비범한). 글 전체 구조: ordinary를 extraordinary로 변환

questions.stem:
다음 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어 문장을 완성하시오.

조건: 'as if' 구문을 사용하여 "감상자들은 마치 시각적 게임을 하는 것 같은 느낌을 받는다"를 영어로 쓰시오.

Viewers feel __________.
questions.wa: as if they are playing a visual game
accept: as if they are playing a visual game
As if they are playing a visual game
as if they are playing a visual game.
as if they were playing a visual game
as though they are playing a visual game
as though they were playing a visual game

det.korean: 감상자들은 마치 시각적 게임을 하는 것 같은 느낌을 받는다. as if + 주어 + 동사
det.analysis: as if = 마치 ~처럼. Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game. 현재 상황의 비유이므로 현재진행형 또는 가정법(were playing) 모두 가능.
det.tip: as if + S + V = 마치 ~처럼. feel as if = ~인 것 같은 느낌이 들다. as though도 동일한 의미로 사용 가능
